messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: More glitches/questions
parts:
A few more questions/glitches/possible misunderstandings....

* Here's a difference between mapped and set values -- I don't know if
it is by design. It seems that set values do not affect the scale's
range calculation, while mapped ones do:

ggplot(data.frame(x=0:1,y=0:1)) +
geom_rect(aes(x=x,y=y,ymin=-3),xmin=.1,xmax=.2,ymax=3000)

has a y-range of -3 .. 1 (ignoring the 3000).

* About annotate, I couldn't find it in the book -- I guess it's new with 0.8.3?

Unlike 'set' values, annotate values *do* affect the range
calculation, which makes them less handy/useful in the case of
background rectangles defining zones. How can I get them auto-clipped
to the display area?

* On the other hand, if the set y-range (which doesn't affect ranges)
is infinite (I did this not because I was testing corner cases but
because it was the logical thing to do when the band does not have any
vertical limits), no rectangle is plotted at all:

ggplot(data.frame(x=0:1,y=0:1)) +
geom_rect(aes(x=x,y=y),xmin=.1,xmax=.2,ymin=-Inf,ymax=Inf)

* It appears that xlim cancels the effect of scale...log10:

ggplot(ddd) + geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y)) + xlim(1,3)+ scale_x_log10()
# log scale, limits set
ggplot(ddd) + geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y)) + scale_x_log10() + xlim(1,3)
# linear scale, limits set

In the first case, the changes to the scale are cumulative; in the
second, xlim cancels log10, as though it had an implicit linear scale.
Is this intentional? Is it documented?

* In the case of size, mapped sizes are (very reasonably) scaled by
the system. 'Set' sizes seem to scale as some sort of proportion of
the plotted range; is the behavior documented somewhere?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: More glitches/questions
parts:
> * Here's a difference between mapped and set values -- I don't know if
> it is by design.  It seems that set values do not affect the scale's
> range calculation, while mapped ones do:
>
>  ggplot(data.frame(x=0:1,y=0:1)) +
>  geom_rect(aes(x=x,y=y,ymin=-3),xmin=.1,xmax=.2,ymax=3000)
>
> has a y-range of -3 .. 1 (ignoring the 3000).

Yes, again because it's the scales that control the range of the axes,
and scales never see the set values. I'm not sure whether this is an
appealing feature or not, but it's unlikely to change.
> * About annotate, I couldn't find it in the book -- I guess it's new with 0.8.3?

> Unlike 'set' values, annotate values *do* affect the range
> calculation, which makes them less handy/useful in the case of
> background rectangles defining zones.  How can I get them auto-clipped
> to the display area?

Oh, hmmm, I hadn't thought about that. You could just the maximum and
minimum ranges of the data? And then use expand = c(0,0) in the x and
y scales.

> * On the other hand, if the set y-range (which doesn't affect ranges)
> is infinite (I did this not because I was testing corner cases but
> because it was the logical thing to do when the band does not have any
> vertical limits), no rectangle is plotted at all:
>
>   ggplot(data.frame(x=0:1,y=0:1)) +
>   geom_rect(aes(x=x,y=y),xmin=.1,xmax=.2,ymin=-Inf,ymax=Inf)

I suspect this is due to how the rectangles are drawn by grid. I'll
look into it.

> * It appears that xlim cancels the effect of scale...log10:
>
>  ggplot(ddd) + geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y)) + xlim(1,3)+ scale_x_log10()
> # log scale, limits set
>  ggplot(ddd) + geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y)) + scale_x_log10() + xlim(1,3)
> # linear scale, limits set
>
> In the first case, the changes to the scale are cumulative; in the
> second, xlim cancels log10, as though it had an implicit linear scale.
>  Is this intentional? Is it documented?

Currently xlim(1,3) is just a short cut for scale_x_continuous(limits
= c(1,3)) which would be overridden by scale_x_log10. (Although the
order shouldn't matter - I don't know why you'd be seeing a
difference). I have plans to implement xlim in a different way, which
would overcome this problem.

> * In the case of size, mapped sizes are (very reasonably) scaled by
> the system.  'Set' sizes seem to scale as some sort of proportion of
> the plotted range; is the behavior documented somewhere?

Set sizes are in mm. This should be documented in the specifications
appendix of the book.

Hadley
